findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The facility has a TIME AS CONTROL policy in place for foods on the breakfast buffet, but the employee stated that they have been keeping some items to save on food cost. The following TCS food items were observed to be above 41F:

1. Waffle batter probed to be at 48F. Waffle batters are cold held using ice packs on the sides of the dispenser, which does not allow for proper cold holding below 41F. The employee stated that they have been putting the leftover waffle batters in the cooler to use for the next day. Cease doing this, as the waffle batters are not being properly cold held at below 41F and the package states to refrigerate the batter after it is made. 
2. There are two cold holding buffet lines that are cold held using ice below the containers. Cantaloupe probed to be at 47F and yogurt probed to be at 50F on one line. Cottage cheese probed to be at 48F, tomatoes probed to be at 47F, and watermelon probed to be at 50F on the second cold holding line. The employee stated that they had been saving the leftovers of these items. It was discussed to discard the leftovers after breakfast and to place less of the items out if wanting to save on food cost. 
3. There are two milk carafes, one containing 2% milk and the other containing almond milk. The employee stated that they place these back in the cooler after breakfast and the containers are emptied and cleaned every other day. Cease this practice. The milks should be discarded after breakfast and the containers should be cleaned daily. 

TIME AS CONTROL should be used for the breakfast buffet, as the facility does not have the equipment that allows for proper cold holding at 41F and below. The PIC stated that their policy is to use time as control. Ensure that all staff are educated on this and are being trained to discard items after breakfast. Ensure that TCS foods are being held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Illinois adopted the 2022 FDA Food Code which requires bulk/buffet items in establishments to have the major allergens listed on them. The items on the buffet need to have the major allergens listed in some form. This can be accomplished by a picture of the allergen outside of each one, a poster that lists the allergen next to each food item, or another form that clearly communicates the allergens container to the consumer.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.
